items.item_text: Current California Pharmacist license in good standing
Board Certification in Pharmacotherapy (BCPS)
Minimum 2 years of hospital inpatient pharmacy experience or completion of an accredited residency
Experience developing and implementing clinical pharmacy programs and performance improvement initiatives
Experience providing drug information, clinical education, and in-service programs
Prior supervisory or clinical leadership experience

You bring more than skill, knowledge, and expertise to your role as an allied health professional. You bring a deep passion for improving the lives of everyone around you. At UCLA Health, we’re committed to fostering a working environment where you are supported and empowered to be your best. You’ll love it here!

Join UCLA Health as a Clinical Manager, a key leadership role within Pharmacy Services at Ronald Reagan UCLA Medical Center. Reporting to the Director of Pharmacy, you will be responsible for the overall development, implementation, and oversight of clinical pharmacy programs while supporting the professional growth and competency development of clinical pharmacy staff.

In this role, you will lead clinical and performance improvement initiatives related to medication use, drug therapy optimization, and cost containment. You will collaborate closely with medical staff, nursing, and interdisciplinary teams to develop and implement clinical pharmacy programs that align with departmental and medical center goals. You will also ensure timely communication of new and updated policies, procedures, and clinical practices. You will provide operational and clinical leadership by ensuring services are delivered in compliance with departmental policies, regulatory standards, and accreditation requirements. This includes serving as a liaison between pharmacy and nursing teams, supporting budget adherence, and identifying opportunities to improve efficiency, safety, and quality of care.

At UCLA Health, passionate clinicians in a wide range of disciplines have enabled us to become a world-renowned health system with four award-winning hospitals and more than 270 community clinics throughout Southern California. We’re also home to the world-class medical research and clinical education capabilities of the David Geffen School of Medicine. If you’re looking to experience greater challenge and fulfillment in your career, come to UCLA Health.
(Commensurate with experience and aligned with internal equity)
Doctor of Pharmacy (PharmD) from an accredited school of pharmacy
Preferred Qualifications:
Commitment to patient-centered care, professionalism, and UCLA Health policies and standards
ASHP-accredited residency
Active participation in professional pharmacy organizations

the final candidate who accepts an offer of employment will be required to disclose if they have been subject to any final administrative or judicial decisions within the last seven years determining that they committed any misconduct; or have filed an appeal of a finding of substantiated misconduct with a previous employer.
Strong knowledge of state and federal pharmacy regulations, accreditation standards, and departmental policies
Ability to collaborate effectively with physicians, nursing staff, and interdisciplinary teams
Demonstrated ability to prioritize multiple projects, identify problems, and recommend effective solutions
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including policy and procedure development
Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced clinical environment with frequent interruptions
